planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, humus-rich soil in full shade to part sun; offsets fill in a 12-inch clump within about two seasons.

directions: A diminutive Chinese relative of Solomon's seal with glossy, almost waxy dark green leaves on gently arching stems that stay evergreen in milder climates. Pendulous pure white bell flowers open in mid-spring and last a long time, later giving way to dark, attractive berries. It is vigorous for a woodland groundcover, throwing off several new offsets a year in average, humus-rich soil with average to moist conditions. Pair it with hostas, Maianthemum, or Disporum as an easy-care, low evergreen edge along a shaded path.

planting.note: Divide and transplant in spring into humus-rich soil, siting in full shade in warm climates or more sun in cooler ones, and mulch well since the very late buds need protection from hard frost.

directions: A Japanese collector's selection of Fortune's saxifrage grown as much for foliage as flower: new leaves emerge lime-green edged in burgundy and covered in fine burgundy hairs, darkening further as the season progresses. In September and October it sends up uniquely shaped brilliant pink flowers with primrose-yellow anthers, late enough that colder gardens should mulch to protect the buds from frost. It forms tight, quickly multiplying clumps about a foot across and tolerates both full sun and full shade, though some shade is kinder in hot climates.
